title: Custom Priority: PriorityQueue with Custom Comparators
summary: Control queue priority using custom Comparator lambdas: implementing Max-Heaps, multi-level priority (urgency + timestamp), and hospital triage queues.

activities.title: Practical Context: Air Traffic Controller Landing Stacks

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Air Traffic Controller Landing Stacks
analogy.story:
Air traffic control centers hold inbound aircraft in holding stacks. Primary priority is assigned by fuel reserves: an aircraft with a 'Mayday - Fuel Low' transponder code preempts all standard scheduled flights (Primary tier).

If two aircraft hold identical fuel status, the flight that entered the regional airspace perimeter first receives landing clearance first (FIFO tie-breaker). This multi-tier protocol prevents starvation while averting disasters.
analogy.keyTakeaway: Real-world priority decisions rely on compound rules: primary urgency criteria combined with deterministic secondary tie-breakers.

activities.title: Custom Comparators, Max-Heaps, and Tie-Breaking Invariants

keyTakeaways: Passing Collections.reverseOrder() or (a, b) -> b.compareTo(a) transforms PriorityQueue into a Max-Heap
Compound comparators chain .comparingInt().thenComparingLong() for multi-level priority evaluation
Never subtract integers (a - b) in comparators; integer underflow/overflow causes catastrophic sign inversion
PriorityQueue is NOT stable by default: tie-breaking equal priorities requires explicit monotonic sequence numbers

activities.content:
### Constructing Max-Heaps in PriorityQueue

By default, `PriorityQueue` roots the smallest element (`compare(parent, child) <= 0`). To create a **Max-Heap** where the largest element occupies the root:
1. `Collections.reverseOrder()`: Inverts the natural ordering of `Comparable` objects.
2. Lambda / Method Reference: `(a, b) -> Integer.compare(b, a)` or `Comparator.reverseOrder()`.

---

### The Integer Overflow Subtraction Anti-Pattern

A critical bug in junior Java implementations is using subtraction in comparators:
```java
// SEVERE BUG: Fails on numeric boundary extremes!
Comparator<Integer> broken = (a, b) -> a - b;
// If a = -2_000_000_000 and b = 1_000_000_000:
// a - b underflows to +1_294_967_296, falsely claiming a > b!
```
Always use static helper methods:
```java
Comparator<Integer> safe = Integer::compare;
Comparator<Long> safeLong = Long::compare;
```

---

### Deterministic FIFO Tie-Breaking

`PriorityQueue` is **not stable**. When two elements evaluate to `compare(a, b) == 0`, heap rebalancing makes no guarantee about which element will be polled first. In enterprise job dispatchers, when two jobs share identical priority scores, fairness dictates FIFO dispatch.
To guarantee stability, attach a monotonic sequence counter (`long sequenceId`) to every task and chain:
```java
Comparator<Task> stableComparator = Comparator
    .comparingInt(Task::getPriority)
    .thenComparingLong(Task::getSequenceId);
```

---

### Executable Demonstration: Production Incident Triage

questions.question: What is the primary danger of using (a, b) -> a - b as a Comparator for integers?
options: Numeric underflow or overflow can flip the sign of the subtraction result, corrupting the heap
It forces the PriorityQueue to sort in descending order
questions.explanation: If a is Integer.MIN_VALUE and b is positive, a - b underflows and wraps around to a positive integer, incorrectly stating that a > b. Always use Integer.compare(a, b).

questions.question: How do you configure PriorityQueue to function as a Max-Heap?
options: Pass Collections.reverseOrder() or (a, b) -> b.compareTo(a) to the constructor
Use the MaxPriorityQueue class from java.util.concurrent
questions.explanation: PriorityQueue takes an optional Comparator in its constructor. Passing Collections.reverseOrder() reverses the natural order, transforming it into a Max-Heap.

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: Achieving FIFO Stability in PriorityQueue

qaList.question: Java's PriorityQueue is documented as non-stable. If two incoming tasks have the exact same priority value, how do you architect a PriorityQueue that strictly guarantees FIFO dispatch order among equals?
qaList.answer: To guarantee FIFO stability in a PriorityQueue: wrap each task inside an OrderedTask container that attaches an incrementing monotonic sequence number (private static final AtomicLong SEQ = new AtomicLong(); private final long seq = SEQ.getAndIncrement();). Supply a compound comparator: Comparator.comparing(OrderedTask::getPriority).thenComparingLong(OrderedTask::getSeq). Because the sequence counter is strictly monotonically increasing, no two objects will ever evaluate as equal. When business priorities match, the lower sequence number (earlier arrival) strictly wins, guaranteeing deterministic FIFO ordering.

practiceProblems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements using a min-heap PriorityQueue ordered by frequency. Achieve O(N log K) time complexity.

practiceProblems.title: K Closest Points to Origin
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given an array of points where points[i] = [x_i, y_i] represents a point on the X-Y plane and an integer k, return the k closest points to the origin (0, 0) using a max-heap of size k.

practiceProblems.title: Deterministic Stable FIFO Priority Dispatcher
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a StablePriorityQueue<T> that accepts elements with an integer priority and guarantees that elements with the same priority are polled strictly in First-In, First-Out (FIFO) arrival order.

practiceProblems.title: Reorganize String to Prevent Adjacent Duplicates
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given a string s, rearrange the characters of s so that any two adjacent characters are not the same. Return any possible rearrangement, or return empty string "" if not possible. Use a max-heap tracking character frequencies.

practiceProblems.title: Continuous Median from Data Stream (Two Heaps)
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a MedianFinder class that calculates the median of numbers dynamically added to a stream in O(log N) insertion time and O(1) median query time using two heaps: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.
